Anti-folk - Wikipedia
Contents
Anti-folk
Anti-folk
(sometimes spelled
antifolk
) is a
genre
of
folk music
that emerged in the 1980s in New York City. It was founded by singer-songwriter
Lach
, as a response to the prevailing folk music scene.
[
1
]
It is characterized by its amateur sound,
DIY ethos
, and often humorous, rebellious, or satirical lyrics. Antifolk music was made to diverge from, and sometimes mock, the perceived seriousness of the era's mainstream music scene,
[
2
]
while often still being
protest music
aimed at social change.
[
3
]
[
4
]
The latter element especially overlaps with
folk punk
.
History
Antifolk began as Lach's response to being barred from
Greenwich Village
folk clubs such as
Folk City
and The Speakeasy because his music crossed folk with punk.
[
5
]
In the early 1980s, singer-songwriter
Lach
started The Fort,
[
6
]
an after-hours club on NYC's
Rivington Street
on the
Lower East Side
.
[
7
]
The Fort's opening coincided with the New York Folk Festival. Because of this, Lach dubbed his event the
New York Antifolk Festival
.
[
8
]
Other early proponents of the movement included
the Washington Squares
,
Cindy Lee Berryhill
,
Brenda Kahn
,
Paleface
,
Beck
,
Hamell on Trial
,
Michelle Shocked
, Zane Campbell,
John S. Hall
,
[
9
]
[
10
]
Roger Manning
,
[
11
]
Kirk Kelly
.
[
12
]
The original Fort was shut down in 1985 by the police, and because of this the club moved locations several times, including
East Village
bars Sophie's and Chameleon, before settling in the back room of the
SideWalk Cafe
starting in 1993.
[
7
]
[
8
]
The
New York Antifolk Festival
was held annually at the
SideWalk Cafe
until its closure in 2019 (long outlasting the original Folk Festival).
[
13
]
Events have also taken place in the
band shells
in
Tompkins Square Park
and
Central Park
.
[
8
]
While living in San Francisco in the early 1990s, Lach helped establish a West Coast anti-folk movement at the Sacred Grounds Coffee House.
[
7
]
Other artists to have achieved a notable level of success who have been considered anti-folk include
Jeffrey Lewis
,
Regina Spektor
and
the Moldy Peaches
.
[
14
]
[
15
]
[
16
]
In the 2000s the term was adopted in Britain, particularly in the London underground scene, with acts including
David Cronenberg's Wife
and The Bobby McGee's.
[
17
]
The UK antifolk scene, largely centred in London and
Brighton
, has established its own identity, which was written about in a six-page feature in the September 2007 issue of
Plan B
magazine.
[
18
]
In 2004 the
lo-fi
musician
Filthy Pedro
started seasonal anti-folk festivals, which he promoted with Tom Mayne of the band David Cronenberg's Wife.
[
19
]
An anti-folk scene in Brighton, curated primarily by Mertle, was quick to follow that of London.
Other key figures within the UK anti-folk community include
Dan Treacy
of Television Personalities,
Jack Hayter
, Milk Kan,
Extradition Order
,
Benjamin Shaw
, Lucy Joplin, Candythief, JJ Crash, Larry Pickleman and
Paul Hawkins
.
[
citation needed
]
Emmy the Great
and
Laura Marling
were added to the roster of antifolk artists as they play antifolk music with mocking lyrics.
[
20
]
Kate Nash
started her music career playing anti-folk-style shows, including a concert promoted by Larry Pickleman and Mertle in Brighton.
[
21
]
Dan Willson, who performs under the name
Withered Hand
, is an Edinburgh-based musician often considered part of the genre. His first studio album,
Good News
, was released in 2009.
[
22
]
Welsh antifolk artist Mr Duke has gained some popularity in Wales, and
Crywank
, an antifolk project from Manchester, surfaced in 2009.
